description: Composite two-panel figure that pairs a calculated phase-fraction diagram with a processing-route flow schematic. (a) plots "Volume fraction of all phases" (y-axis, 0.0-1.0) against "Temperature (°C)" (x-axis, 600-1500 with ticks every 150 °C) for four curves keyed by the legend: Liquid (red), Ferrite (black), Austenite (blue), TiB2 (gold). The austenite curve forms a broad plateau just below the 0.9 level between roughly 750 and 950 °C and falls to zero at about 1120 °C; the ferrite curve is low near 600 °C, drops to zero around 700 °C, then rises to a dome-shaped maximum near 0.85 at about 1000 °C before vanishing at ~1130 °C; the TiB2 curve stays low and nearly constant (~0.15) up to ~1000 °C and decreases to zero near 1400 °C; the liquid curve is zero until ~1120 °C, rises steeply and reaches 1.0 by ~1400 °C, remaining fully liquid to 1500 °C. (b) is a four-stage labelled process flow linked by blue chevron arrows: Induction melting (crucible marked Fe, Al, Mn, B, Ti with blue spheres) → Casting (grey rectangular ingot) → Forging and homogenization (press with a red-hot disc) → Hot rolling (two rolls deforming a red slab). Together the panels show that equilibrium phase calculations guided the alloy design so that a TiB2 + (δ-ferrite + austenite) microstructure is produced by induction melting, casting, homogenization/forging and hot rolling.

subfigures.description: Calculated equilibrium phase-fraction diagram: volume fraction of all phases (0.0-1.0) versus Temperature (°C), 600-1500, with four curves labelled Liquid (red), Ferrite (black), Austenite (blue) and TiB2 (gold). Austenite plateaus below 0.9 over ~750-950 °C and disappears near 1120 °C; ferrite shows a dome with a maximum near 0.85 at ~1000 °C; TiB2 is a low nearly constant fraction (~0.15) below ~1000 °C; liquid appears above ~1120 °C and reaches 1.0 by ~1400 °C.

Schematic of the processing route with four stages joined by blue chevron arrows: Induction melting (crucible labelled Fe, Al, Mn, B, Ti with blue spheres) → Casting (rectangular ingot) → Forging and homogenization (pressing apparatus acting on a red-hot disc) → Hot rolling (two rolls deforming a red-hot slab).

observations.observation: Panel (a) is a phase-fraction versus temperature calculation with y-axis labelled 'Volume fraction of all phases' (0.0 to 1.0) and x-axis labelled 'Temperature (°C)' running from 600 to 1500.
The four legend entries in panel (a) are Liquid (red), Ferrite (black/grey), Austenite (blue) and TiB2 (gold).
In panel (a) the austenite (blue) curve plateaus at roughly 0.85 between about 750 and 950 °C and falls to zero at about 1120 °C.
In panel (a) the ferrite (black) curve is low at 600 °C, falls to zero near 700 °C, then rises to a dome maximum of about 0.85 near 1000 °C before dropping to zero at roughly 1130 °C.
In panel (a) the TiB2 (gold) curve remains a low, nearly constant fraction (about 0.15) from 600 to ~1000 °C and decreases towards zero near 1400 °C.
In panel (a) the liquid (red) curve is zero up to about 1120 °C, then rises steeply to a value of 1.0 at about 1400 °C and stays at 1.0 up to 1500 °C.

Panel (b) is a process-flow schematic whose stages, in arrow order, are 'Induction melting' (crucible labelled Fe, Al, Mn, B, Ti with blue spheres), 'Casting' (grey rectangular ingot), 'Forging and homogenization' (press with a red-hot disc) and 'Hot rolling' (two rolls with a red hot slab).
The figure caption states that (a) shows volume fractions of equilibrium phases from phase diagram calculations and (b) shows a schematic of the processing routes.

The citing text states the alloy was a 50 kg vacuum-induction-melted ingot of nominal composition Fe-15.5Mn-3.95Al-5Ti-2.15B (wt. %), chosen to give 14 vol. % TiB2 in a δ-ferrite plus austenite matrix, determined from Fig. 1(a) using Thermo-Calc with the TCFE9 database.

The citing text describes the processing sequence as homogenization at 1373 K for two hours, then hot rolling in the two-phase region in five steps with a finishing temperature of 1173 K to a 3 mm thick sheet, followed by air cooling to room temperature, matching the stages drawn in panel (b).
The citing text states the actual measured composition of the rolled sheet was Fe-16Mn-3.9Al-5.11Ti-2.09B (wt. %).
The citing text states that Al addition promotes formation of δ-ferrite, which initially formed during solidification as shown in Fig. 1(a) and was inherited during subsequent hot rolling.
